primary_cause: Evidence is conflicting: reports describe stronger Capesize rates and demand during 2026, while BIMCO-related reporting says the apparent strength was substantially driven by forced rerouting and may reverse as a supply glut develops. The evidence does not establish a durable commodity-volume dry-bulk cycle.
counter_evidence: BIMCO warned that 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial, driven by forced rerouting, and that a 2027 supply glut could reverse the benefit. [Dry Bulk Shipping Faces 2027 Supply Glut: BIMCO Warns Hormuz Rerouting Boost Will Reverse] https://www.techtimes.com/articles/322617/20260801/dry-bulk-shipping-faces-2027-supply-glut-bimco-warns-hormuz-rerouting-boost-will-reverse.htm
source_summary: A key measure of bulk-shipping rates reached its highest level since December 2023, attributed to rising Capesize demand and tightening vessel supply. [Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand] https://gcaptain.com/dry-bulk-shipping-rates-hit-two-year-high-on-capesize-demand/

primary_cause: Current evidence indicates storage demand and NAND-related activity, but it does not provide sufficiently precise, time-consistent confirmation of NAND pricing, controller/module demand, or inventory normalization. The available material is also not sufficiently independent for a confident causal classification.
counter_evidence: A storage-industry analysis argued that NAND supply may not be able to catch demand in the same way as prior cycles, implying structural changes rather than a clearly established conventional pricing and inventory cycle.
